newsitem.title: USA: Ex-senator to aid utilities seeking deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Ex-senator to aid utilities seeking deregulation.

text.p: Former U.S. senator Bennett Johnston of Louisiana signed on to work with a group of utilities pressing for deregulation of the electric industry, the Alliance for Competitive Electricity said Friday.

Johnston, who just retired from the Senate, was the top Democrat on the Senate Energy Committee for 16 years and was the first lawmaker to introduce a broad electric deregulation bill in Congress last year.
The alliance said he would help it craft policy recommendations and "provide strategic advice".

"I am delighted to be able to work with a group that shares a vision of working with all stakeholders to guarantee the widest possible benefit of a more competitive system of electricity generation," Johnston said in a statement.
He also announced Friday that he was setting up a Washington-based business consulting firm with his son, Hunter, and two former Senate staffers.
The Johnstons also planned to form a separate firm to pursue energy infrastructure investments in the United States and abroad.
